question: Can source-literal candidate extraction and evidence-linked composition repair policy rules, then preserve selective revision behavior on new documents?
development: The prior 32 authored controls and 16 Yangsan/Yongin claims have been observed. All development comparisons are post-hoc. Reuse their profile/direct outputs and claim-grounding method.
methods: source-literal candidates plus a restricted deterministic conjunction/explicit-any baseline
same candidates composed by each local model
one source-only feedback repair for malformed, missing-candidate or mechanically inconsistent compositions; no claim/reference labels
scope_dependency: Scope text remains manually selected and can resolve exclusion polarity; report this explicitly. Candidate literals are grounded mechanically, their meaning and logical composition are not independently verified.
iteration: Measure candidate coverage and rule errors separately. If repair fails, retain failures and run a distinct declared follow-up, without overwriting frozen results.
new_documents: Freeze method before searching new sources. Target at least 2 previously unread official document families, 4 scopes and 16 authored claims with monetary and non-monetary conditions. Preserve scoped and wider-context comparisons separately.
revision_integration: Apply policy/fact reading to before/after documents already held in the selective-update study, evaluate changed rules and changed applicant conclusions, including previously wrong stored answers. This is integration on old sources, not a new independent document test.
stop_work: Complete executable corrections and diagnostics, source-referenced counterexamples, new-source transfer, revision integration, reproducibility and both repository/Pages publication. Do not label remaining model failures solved. Independent human adjudication requires external participants and is not simulated.
